payload.statement:
# Problem: Council review of Chapter 5, Classes (quarto-book/chapters/05-classes.qmd)

You are the hol-rulebook council. Audit this chapter as a publishable unit of the Heroes of Legend
TTRPG rulebook and produce a disposition plan. Do NOT fix anything; file findings only.

## Scope
The registered source `05-classes` (the chapter's .qmd). Cross-check against the rest of the book where
a claim is canon-determined (skill roster ch07, core resolution/boon-bane ch06, combat/conditions ch13,
disciplines/ladder/budget ch08, advancement/DP economy ch18, talents ch09, character-creation templates
ch02, spell catalogs ch11/ch12, glossary ch21, reference sheets ch22). The chapter covers: the nine
classes (Protector, Blade, Arcanist, Shepherd, Intellect, Odd, Leader, Unbalanced, Shadow) with L1
disciplines, signatures, favored skills, starting kits, per-class Discipline cost tables; the class
archetype table (four archetypes + Odd); the per-class ability tables (10 abilities each, Novice/Adept/
Master ladder); and the Progression + Costs sections (card costs 2/4/8, Home/Adjacent/Foreign/Opposed
structures, comprehensive cost table).

## Locked conventions the chapter must satisfy (cite the violated convention in every finding)
- **Damage budget = FLAT numbers, on the table, no dice.** Novice 2/4/6, Adept 6/9/12, Master 9/15/21
  (Weak/Standard/Strong). "The table is the law." Every damaging/healing number must be a budget row, an
  explicit Basic-card floor, a damage-TIER bump ("+1 damage tier"), or an on-row conditional rider that
  SUMS to a row. Recurring HoT totals over the stated duration = the row.
- **ZERO flat +N damage riders (weapons rework, 2026-08-19, book-wide).** Any "deals +N damage",
  "+N bonus damage", "gains +N damage" is DEAD anywhere in the book, including class abilities. The
  canonical way to raise damage is "+1 damage tier (one row up on the damage budget)".
- **Ladder discipline:** Novice = 1 disc (or no prereq), Adept = EXACTLY 2, Master = EXACTLY 3 (max 3
  ever; shapes 3 different / 2+1 / 3 same).
- **Level gates (canon, ch18:45):** Adept unlocks at Level 3, Master at Level 7.
- **DP economy (final, #195, ch18):** cards flat 2/4/8 DP; per-level DP awards 3-4 with carry-over
  (ch18:39, PR #385: "Unspent DP carries over to your next level"). Any ch05 text about spending DP must
  not contradict carry-over.
- **Boon/Bane (ch06):** Boon = roll 4d6 keep the highest three; Bane = roll 4d6 keep the lowest three.
- **Conditions vocabulary (ch13 table):** leveled conditions use the "Name X" form (Dazed X, Poisoned X,
  Slowed X, Burning X, Frozen X); binary conditions by name (Frightened, Prone, Restrained, Invisible...).
  Bespoke near-conditions ("rooted", "Fear effect") that duplicate or drift from the table are findings.
- **One-roll principle (ch13, locked):** the hit/attack roll IS the roll; no second roll unless the card
  explicitly invokes the sanctioned 3d6 or boon-bane 4d6 mechanics.
- **Style law: ZERO em-dashes** in prose. No damage dice anywhere (the only sanctioned dice: 3d6
  one-rolls, 4d6 boon/bane, and explicit random-behavior tables such as a class signature's d6 backlash
  table or a 1d4 random-effect table, which are not damage rolls).
- **Cross-references:** @sec-* links must resolve; every ability named in prose (e.g. a signature that
  grants a named ability) must exist in the book's tables; every spell named in an ability effect must
  exist in ch11/ch12.
- **Cost tables:** the nine per-class Discipline cost tables and the comprehensive cost table must agree
  cell-for-cell; every class must have a coherent Home/Adjacent/Foreign/Opposed distribution.

## Findings format (one finding per member this round)
Each finding must be decision-oriented: name the broken value with [05-classes:LINE], the
expected/correct value, the violated convention, and the minimal fix. Cite cross-chapter canon lines where
the expected value is canon-determined. Severity is implicit in the fix size. Do NOT invent defects to
look thorough; a chapter with few real problems is a good outcome.

payload.argument: Chapter 5 is a coherent publishable unit in structure (nine classes, archetype grouping, 10-row ability tables each, progression and cost sections) but carries 8 verified defects. MECHANICAL (chapter-local, zero mechanics change): [05-classes:603] denies Development-Point carry-over while ch18:39 establishes carry-over as final economy; fix the sentence to affirm carry-over. [05-classes:501] uses a removed status wording instead of the Frightened entry in the ch13 table; [05-classes:508-509] repeat the same non-table status name twice; fix all three to the ch13 vocabulary. [05-classes:471] grants a flat +2 damage rider, dead under the book-wide zero-flat-rider law; replace with one damage tier. [05-classes:346] backlash table row 5 adds a flat +2 to the target; same law, same fix. SUBSTANTIVE (content or cross-chapter reconciliation): [05-classes:88] the Blade signature grants a named ability that exists in no table in the book (also referenced at ch02:449); add a budget-compliant row to the Blade table or drop the reference. [05-classes:576] Unmake cites a disintegration spell absent from the ch11/ch12 catalogs; add the Master spell or rewrite the effect self-contained. [05-classes:433-436] the archetype table's Ability Pool column claims 8/8/9/6 while the actual tables hold exactly 10 rows per class (verified programmatically, 90 total); recompute or redefine the column. DESIGN-DECISION: [05-classes:562] invents a bespoke speed-zero status; adopt the table's Restrained (which adds an attack penalty the current text lacks) or register a new condition in ch13. Verified clean: ladder discipline 0 violations across all 90 rows, level gates match ch18 (Adept 3, Master 7), all @sec links resolve, all favored skills exist in the ch07 roster, Corruption and Morale check mechanics are canon-anchored, and flat damage numbers in ability rows all sit on budget rows.

payload.argument: The chapter's published rule set is not self-contained: two of its signature and ability effects point at content that does not exist in the book, so the text as written is unplayable for those entries. The strongest counter-example is the Unbalanced class's Master ability Unmake, whose effect is defined purely by delegating to a named spell that I could not find anywhere: the spell appears in neither the arcane catalog (thirty entries, chapter 11), the divine catalog (chapter 12), nor any other file in the repo. With no entry to read, the ability has no defined damage, range, save, or resurrection exception; the only mechanically resolvable result is the two Corruption it grants. The same dangling-reference failure, at higher frequency, is the Blade signature Swift Blade, which tells the player they gain a named ability. That ability has no row in the Blade table (ten other abilities are listed there), no row in any other class table, and no standalone definition; a character created from the signature is promised a named ability with no tier, cost, trigger, or numbers, and the chapter-2 template describes it differently from this line, so even the intent is ambiguous. Two further violations survive my stress-test. The Edge of Chaos backlash table row 5 applies a flat numeric damage increase to the target, the exact flat-plus-N rider form the book bans in favor of a tier bump. And the Progression section's claim that Development Points are forfeited if unspent directly contradicts chapter 18's explicit carry-forward rule, which the locked conventions mark as final. The cost tables I checked cell-for-cell (nine class tables versus the comprehensive table, plus the four-structure ladder) are internally coherent, and the Odd pool and archetype counts are consistent; the defects are the dangling references and the two rider/economy lines, not the tables.

payload.argument: Audited ch05's concrete mechanics against the rest of the book. Verified clean: the nine per-class Discipline cost tables agree cell-for-cell with the comprehensive cost table (extracted both and diffed programmatically, 207 cells compared, zero disagreements); all three @sec cross-references resolve to existing anchors; all 80 non-Odd ability rows satisfy the ladder (Novice 0-1 disc, Adept exactly 2, Master exactly 3, ranks summed); every flat damage and healing value in an effect matches the ch08 budget row for its tier, including tier-bump targets; the 23-discipline roster matches ch21 exactly; no em-dashes; all starting-kit items are purchasable at L1 with no unbuyable-discipline requirement; Boon and Bane usage matches ch06 and ch21. Broken items, each with a minimal fix: (1) [05-classes:88] the Blade signature grants an ability named Precise Stab, but that name has no defining table anywhere in the book (only mirrored at 02-character-creation:449), so the promised effect is undefined. Expected: a table row defining it (Blade table or ch09 talents) or an inline effect; mechanical fix. (2) [05-classes:576] Unmake says the target dies per the Disintegrate spell, but no spell by that name exists in ch11, ch12, or any chapter. Expected: add the spell to ch11 or reword the effect inline; mechanical fix. (3) [05-classes:603] Progression says level DP must all be spent and never carries over, directly contradicting the locked ch18 economy (ch18:39: unspent DP carries over, saving toward an 8 DP purchase is stated strategy). Fix: reword to match ch18; mechanical fix. (4) [05-classes:471] Leverage adds a flat numeric damage bonus, the one flat-damage rider in the chapter, which the locked zero-riders convention bans book-wide; every comparable line here uses the canonical one-tier-up phrasing. Fix: replace with a one-tier damage bump; mechanical fix. (5) [05-classes:562] Hold the Line applies a speed-zero state called rooted, a near-condition absent from the ch13 table (closest canon: Restrained, speed 0); also [05-classes:501, 508, 509] use Fear effect and immunity to Fear while ch13's binary condition is Frightened. Fix: standardize on Restrained and Frightened or add the terms to ch13; mechanical fix. (6) [05-classes:433-436] the archetype table's Ability Pool column claims 8/8/9/6, but row-counting each class ability table gives exactly 10 rows per class (80 non-Odd rows), matching neither a per-class nor a shared-pool reading. Fix: recompute the column or define what the pool counts; mechanical fix. (7) [05-classes:392, 398, 529, 536, 541] the Shadow kit and abilities lean on concealment and heavy concealment, a combat state defined nowhere in the book (ch13 defines Cover and the Invisible condition only; the term's only other home is the ch15 smoke bomb) - the Shadow's core loop references an undefined state. Fix: define concealment in ch13 or rekey to the Invisible condition; mechanical fix. All seven are mechanical, none require design decisions.

payload.argument: Audit of Chapter 5 mechanics against the locked conventions: damage numbers, cost tables, prereq shapes, level gates, and dice usage were all verified, and one genuine violation stands. The Intellect Adept ability Leverage (05-classes.qmd:471) grants a fixed +2 flat bonus to the hit's damage when an ally's reroll connects. The 2026-08-19 weapons rework made zero flat +N damage riders book-wide, including in class abilities; the only sanctioned way to raise a hit's damage is a tier bump, one row up on the damage budget (08-disciplines.qmd:172). Broken value: +2 bonus damage. Expected value: +1 damage tier. Minimal fix: replace the flat rider in Leverage's effect with the tier bump. Everything else in the chapter passes: all flat damage and healing numbers (2/4/6, 6/9/12, 9/15/21) sit exactly on budget rows; recurring damage is stated per round matching a row, as the ch13 condition table and ch12's recurring healing both do; every Adept row requires exactly 2 disciplines and every Master row exactly 3; all damage dice are the sanctioned d6 backlash table and 1d4 random-effect table; the nine per-class discipline cost tables agree cell-for-cell with the comprehensive table (only cosmetic asterisk/footnote markers differ); card prices are flat 2/4/8 and the gates read Adept at 3, Master at 7, matching ch18:45. Two soft notes, not counted as findings: line 603 says unspent DP is burned each level, which contradicts the carry-over canon at ch18:39 (expected: unspent DP carries to the next level); and the Blade signature at line 88 names a Precise Stab ability that no table in the book defines, leaving the signature's second half without a mechanical effect.

payload.argument: Voice and consistency mostly hold: all nine class openers carry an italic signature quote, the 'this is not X' construction appears only twice (chapter opener line 13 and the Vanish signature line 392) and reads as a device rather than a tic, and the DA term matches the rest of the book. But four real defects must change before publication. First, the Shepherd's signature shares its exact name with a divine spell in ch12 (05-classes.qmd:172 vs 12-divine-spells.qmd:282), and the two have different effects (armor-ignoring energy vs a morale-cone), so a player or DA cannot tell which one the ch02 template (02-character-creation.qmd:373) is referencing. Second, the Shadow ability 'Fade' (05-classes.qmd:542) collides with the arcane spell 'Fade' (11-arcane-spells.qmd:426). Third, the Protector ability 'Immovable' (05-classes.qmd:558) collides with the magic item 'Immovable Rod' and its granted maneuver 'Immovable' (17-magic-items.qmd:321-327). Fourth, the Progression section (05-classes.qmd:603) tells the reader Development Points do not carry over, which directly contradicts ch18's canonical statement that unspent DP carries to the next level (18-advancement.qmd:41); the chapter's own @sec-chapter-advancement reference makes the contradiction self-inflicted. Smaller: Rallying Cry's 'remove one Fear effect' (05-classes.qmd:501) uses a bespoke near-condition; the ch13 condition table defines Frightened, not Fear. Minimal fixes: rename the Shepherd signature (e.g., 'Unholy Word') or rename the ch12 spell, rename the Shadow ability (e.g., 'Flicker'), rename the Protector ability (e.g., 'Unshakeable'), delete the no-carry-over sentence at line 603 in favor of a pointer to ch18, and swap 'Fear effect' for 'Frightened'. The 'Keyed to X' phrase recurs in six of nine class descriptions (lines 84, 129, 168, 207, 246, 287) with a variant at line 388 and silence in Protector and Unbalanced; I flag this only as an optional harmonization condition, not a demand.

payload.argument: The Progression section of this chapter directly contradicts the canon advancement chapter it points readers to. Line 603 tells heroes to spend every Development Point immediately because leftovers are lost, while 18-advancement.qmd line 39 states that unspent DP rolls into the next level and that banking points toward an 8-DC Master card is an intended strategy. A player relying on this chapter alone would make a materially wrong spending decision, which is a broken cross-reference, not a cosmetic one. Fix: rewrite the second sentence of line 603 to match ch18 (e.g., 'Unspent DP carries over to the next level'). The rest of the chapter's progression summary does agree with ch18: Adept gates at level 3 and Master at level 7 (line 605 vs ch18 lines 45, 51), and the 3-4 DP per level cadence (line 603 vs ch18 line 39). Everything else I audited is structurally clean: all three @sec-* references (lines 37, 444, 603) resolve to existing anchors in the book; all nine ability tables have exactly 10 rows with valid tier ladders (Novice 4-5, Adept 3-4, Master 2-3); the nine class-specific discipline cost tables and the combined cost table (line 624) are complete and line up with one another cell-for-cell; per-class structure is uniform (Signature, L1 disciplines, Favored Skills, Starting Kit); and all eighteen pagebreaks sit immediately before a heading. Two secondary, non-blocking gaps: (a) the nine per-class mindset callouts (lines 73, 112, 157, 196, 235, 276, 315, 377, 418) are written as ## headings, the same level as their parent class, so they render as top-level TOC entries instead of nesting under the class - demote to ###; (b) two named abilities referenced in the chapter are defined nowhere in the book: Precise Stab (line 88, Blade signature, also referenced in ch02 line 449) and the Disintegrate spell (line 576, Unbalanced's Unmake) - each needs a definition or a cross-reference target.

dissent.position: Supported the chapter's structural publishability (nine classes, uniform sections, 10-row tables, progression and cost sections all coherent) while enumerating the same eight verified defects in its disposition; dissent is on the reject verdict, not on any defect or its fix.

payload.rationale: t-01 was voted on by all seven members. Six (contrarian, researcher, game-architect, author, editor-in-chief, layout-expert) refuted the chapter's publishability on concrete, individually verified defects; the librarian's support position (structure is sound, defects are fixable) is recorded as dissent on the verdict, not on the defect list. No finding was rebutted, so the reject-majority (6 >= reject_quorum 4) is terminal per the consensus engine. Every cited line was re-verified by the orchestrator against the source file and, for the layout claims, against the built PDF with pdftotext. The cost-table, ladder, and cross-reference claims were independently re-run programmatically (198 cost cells, 90 ability rows, 3 @sec anchors). The only contested claim, the editor-in-chief's callout-heading finding, was checked against a book-wide sibling survey and excluded as a convention mismatch. No sealed rulings exist, so rulings_applied is empty.
payload.recommendation: Chapter 5 (Classes) is REJECTED as a publishable unit, 6-1 (six un-rebutted refutes against the librarian's support), on a defect set the orchestrator re-verified against canon, the cost tables, and the built PDF. TIER 1 - mechanical, same-day micro-PR, zero mechanics change: (1) 05-classes:603 Progression says 'Spend them all, they don't carry over' while ch18:39 establishes carry-over as the final DP economy (decision #45, PR #385); reword to affirm carry-over. (2) 05-classes:501/508/509 use 'Fear effect' / 'immunity to Fear' but the ch13 condition is Frightened and the book-wide pattern is 'immune to Frightened' (ch20:123, 175, 233); standardize all three. (3) 05-classes:562 Hold the Line applies a bespoke 'rooted (speed 0)' state absent from the ch13 condition table; rewrite to a self-contained effect (cannot move) without inventing a condition.
